oneLineSummary: BSM frameworks (MadGraph/FeynRules/MCHM/Lattice) treat custodial as Lagrangian-level INPUT assumption, not derived property. 5 documented PIVOTS exist for max_commutator~2 failures: 't Hooft self-dual / quaternionic L/R / MCHM coset / bidoublet matrix / eta eta-bar orthogonality. Failed-naive cases appear as pedagogical footnotes (Contino TASI 2010, Panico-Wulzer 2015), not standalone papers.
rootCause: max_commutator~2 typically traces to: (1) missing self-dual/anti-self-dual split (t Hooft eta_{ij}^a); (2) missing quaternionic L/R multiplication identification (q -> uqv^{-1}); (3) Hermiticity convention mix (anti-Hermitian vs i T_a/2).
recommendation: PIVOT A 't Hooft symbols: T_L^a = (1/2) eta^a_{ij} M^{ij}, T_R^a = (1/2) eta-bar^a_{ij} M^{ij} on so(4) basis -- automatically satisfies [T_L, T_R]=0 by t Hooft identities. PIVOT B quaternionic equivalent. MCHM SO(5)/SO(4) coset chain (PIVOT C) for sedenion 16D framework.
references: Sannino et al MWT lattice arXiv:0712.1948
caveats: FeynRules does NOT auto-verify custodial -- wrong embedding silently produces rho!=1. Lattice tests are operationally chiral SU(2)L x SU(2)R observables (Goldstone degeneracy, Weinberg sum rules), not algebra commutators.
